http_server.summary: mlflow.server:app Flask application. Two distinct request-input mechanisms: (a) proto-service endpoints registered via app.add_url_rule from get_endpoints(), where handlers parse the body/query via _get_request_message/_get_request_json; (b) flask @app.route endpoints in mlflow/server/__init__.py.

path_relevant_handlers.route: /mlflow-artifacts/artifacts/<path:artifact_path> GET (mlflow/protos/mlflow_artifacts.proto:23-26, registered via app.add_url_rule at mlflow/server/__init__.py:33-34)
path_relevant_handlers.flow: URL path-converter variable -> artifact_repo.download_artifacts(artifact_path) -> open(dst, 'rb') at handlers.py:1441 -> streamed HTTP response

URL path variable -> posixpath.split(artifact_path) -> os.path.join(tmp_dir, tail) -> open(tmp_path, 'wb') at handlers.py:1464 (request body written), then artifact_repo.log_artifact(tmp_path, artifact_path=head)

URL path variable -> artifact_repo.delete_artifacts(artifact_path) -> LocalArtifactRepository.delete_artifacts: os.path.join(artifact_dir, artifact_path) -> shutil.rmtree (mlflow/store/artifact/local_artifact_repo.py:106-112, no normpath and no verify_artifact_path on this path)
request JSON/query parsed into ListArtifacts proto -> request_message.path (handlers.py:898) -> artifact repo list_artifacts(path)
URL path-converter variable -> send_from_directory(STATIC_DIR, path) (Flask safe_join applies)
request artifact_location -> stored experiment artifact root (second-order input; later read back as run.info.artifact_uri by the artifact download/list handlers)

scoring_server.summary: mlflow/pyfunc/scoring_server/__init__.py is a second Flask app, but its HTTP surface only reads flask.request.data / flask.request.content_type (prediction payload and mime type, handlers at lines 211-254); no request field reaches a file path. Its file opens (lines 286, 300) use CLI-supplied --input-path/--output-path in _predict, a local-trusted boundary. Not treated as a path-traversal source boundary.

cli.summary: mlflow/cli.py (click) and _predict(model_uri, input_path, output_path) take paths from the local invoking user; mlflow projects _fetch_project/_unzip_repo URIs likewise come from the CLI/API caller, not from a remote untrusted party. Not extracted as attacker sources; the unzip extractall sink is still extracted because zip entry names are archive-internal untrusted content.

sanitizer_and_validation_evidence: mlflow/store/artifact/artifact_repo.py:302-306 verify_artifact_path(artifact_path) rejects non-normalized, '..'-prefixed, '.' and absolute paths via path_not_unique; applied in LocalArtifactRepository.log_artifact / log_artifacts and HttpArtifactRepository.log_artifact, but NOT on the download/list/delete artifact paths
mlflow/utils/validation.py:82-84 path_not_unique (posixpath.normpath comparison + '..' and '/' prefix rejection)
Flask send_from_directory applies safe_join base-directory containment for serve_static_file
LocalArtifactRepository.download_artifacts/list_artifacts apply os.path.normpath (normalization only, not containment - traversal via '..' segments survives normpath)
TOCTOU note: _send_artifact computes os.path.abspath(artifact_repository.download_artifacts(path)) then send_file reads the path again (handlers.py:438-445)
coverage_gaps: Dynamic dispatch: the server calls artifact_repo.download_artifacts/delete_artifacts/list_artifacts on a base-typed receiver (get_artifact_repository returns whichever repository class the artifact URI scheme resolves to). The extraction captures the concrete LocalArtifactRepository method definitions as boundary params, but flow through other repo subclasses (http, s3, dbfs, ...) is only partially covered by their open/ FS calls.

External-library decoding: querystring_parser.parser.parse and google.protobuf json_format parse_dict are unmodeled external calls; sources are placed at the request.query_string/get_json boundary reads and at the parsed dict/proto field reads instead of modeling taint through these libraries.
Percent-decoding: the raw query string is decoded with .decode('utf-8') and re.sub('%5B%5D',...) before parsing; URL-encoded traversal payloads (e.g. %2e%2e%2f) are not separately modeled.

Alias imports: sinks matched by dotted callee name (open, os.path.getsize, shutil.move, ...) can be missed when a project module re-exports or aliases a stdlib callable (no from X import Y as Z indirection is resolved). No concrete aliasing of FS APIs was observed in the mlflow package.

os.path.join / posixpath.join / os.path.normpath / os.path.abspath / Path.resolve are treated as propagation/validation nodes, NOT sinks, per the extraction policy; they are recorded here as intermediate-node evidence, not candidates.

Path() construction calls (mlflow/artifacts/__init__.py:53, mlflow/models/evaluation/base.py:122,148) use .name/.mkdir on pathlib objects; only the dynamic .mkdir/.read_text/.write_text method-call families are extracted, with inferred module hints.
distutils dir_util.copy_tree receiver 'dir_util' is matched syntactically (from distutils import dir_util at local_artifact_repo.py:1 and projects/utils.py:8).
notes: No route uses Flask Blueprint wrappers; all tracking/registry/artifacts endpoints are registered centrally from proto definitions via app.add_url_rule (mlflow/server/__init__.py:33-34), so source family F2 is keyed on the three concrete handler function names bound to <path:artifact_path> URL rules plus the proto endpoint evidence.
CSV column order matches the previous Path_Traversal projects (gradio et al.): nodeRepr, role, callableName, flowKind, receiver, moduleHint, argIndex, filePath, line, context.
Extraction queries carry no @kind annotation: they are multi-column candidate tables for `codeql query run` + `codeql bqrs decode --format=csv`, not @kind problem queries and not @kind table queries.
